data.title: liquid: enforce no straight lines and no symmetry (blob edges, off-axis layout)

data.body:
Review (audited by script across 320 / 390 / 430 / 768 / 1280, not by eye):

No straight lines — every visible surface's computed border-radius was expanded and each edge's two radii checked to sum to 100%:
- .panel, .chip and all three per-chip radii: ok at every width
- .bloom, .slick, .blob-a (sampled mid-morph, still 100), .hero::before: ok
- The only surfaces left with a uniform radius were the panel and the chips; both are now blobs. Nothing on the page is a rounded rectangle.

No symmetry:
- .content margin at 1280 is 0px / 288px — left-anchored, not 'auto' centred. Page padding 89.6px left vs 40px right.
- Left edges at 1280: serial=111 hero=90 panel=141 elsewhere=103 foot=172. No two blocks share an edge; the staircase holds proportionally at every breakpoint.
- The three chips carry three different radii and three different vertical offsets (margin-top, not transform, so the stagger survives the hover transform).
- Display lines offset 0.22em from each other; bloom and slick given unequal width/height.

No horizontal overflow at any of the five widths. CSS still passes build.js's scoping transform.

Notable decisions:
- clip-path was rejected for the blob shapes: it clips box-shadow, which is what draws the meniscus, the underside and the glow. Documented in BRANDING.md §5.1 so the next agent does not re-derive it.
- Panel padding is expressed in percent, not rem — the inset then tracks the curve at every width, where a fixed rem inset lets text cross the blob on narrow viewports.
- Two iterations were needed on the panel: the first blob (36/30/70/64 vertical split) was bottom-heavy and rendered as a bowl half a page tall, which pushed the footer out of view. Rebalanced to 44/38/62/56 and padding cut from 13% to 7.5/8.5%.

Brief updated in the same pass: §5 became 'Shape, edge and asymmetry' with the pair-sums-to-100 law, the uneven-split rule, the padding consequence and the clip-path warning; §5.2 is the new no-symmetry section; §6 and §9 reconciled (they previously said the column was centred).
